title: Contract algebra: adjoints, reciprocal, and unsat cores
shows: Implication as the adjoint of conjunction, the reciprocal and the quotient as merging with it, adding an assumption or a guarantee, and guarantees that cannot hold when the assumptions do: the contract is compatible and consistent, verify (A & G) fails, and unsat_core gives the terms.

steps.note: Missing is the largest contract that, conjoined with Fast, refines Station: what is still needed besides Fast.
The reciprocal (G, A) is the contract seen from the environment: inputs and outputs exchanged.
The quotient C / C' equals C merged with the reciprocal of C' (Incer et al., arXiv 2309.08875).
Adding an assumption gives an abstraction of the contract.
Adding a guarantee gives a refinement of the contract.

Busy is compatible and consistent (some environment satisfies G req, and A -> G holds when the environment breaks it), but its guarantees cannot hold when its assumptions do: verify checks A & G, which is unsatisfiable.
The core is the assumption G req and the guarantee G (req -> X !req): whenever the environment keeps its promise, the component cannot keep this guarantee. G grant is not in the core.
